analysis:
Examined all supplied BASE scheduler excerpts and the bounded patch against the indexed threat model, including prompt confidentiality, cache isolation, cancellation, admission, output integrity and terminal billing. The visible patch adds GLM media refusal for withheld JSON/forced-tool output (HEAD 512–519) and enables typed reasoning routing for GLM text withholding (HEAD 985–1002). These changes do not independently establish a security regression.
BASE MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift:565–609 reserves media/KV memory; 669–719 binds media cache identity and passes request cache scope; 829–836 and 940–955 preserve scoped text caching (T-041/TB-007). BASE 1022–1085 validates native media controls and installs cancellation-aware forwarding. BASE 1247–1378 drains native media terminal events, preserves typed failure usage and rejects missing terminals; 1401–1487 validates tools/formats before successful terminal usage (T-007, T-010, A-009). Tokenizer resolution and template validation at BASE 1574–1636 were also examined. No supplied change demonstrates weakening encryption, serving authorization, attestation or privileged-helper controls (T-008, T-052/T-053).
Material integration question: only BASE source and a truncated patch are supplied. The complete change map identifies changed output emissions corresponding to BASE 1279–1282, 1392–1395 and 1446–1448, but their replacement implementation is absent. Review HEAD forwarding/withholding logic, GLM5NextPromptPolicy and the relevant parser/validator changes together: confirm invalid JSON or forced calls cannot escape before validation, reasoning stays correctly separated, retained output is bounded, and parser failure/cancellation still reconciles terminal usage and releases leases. Also examine the HEAD test-helper changes at 1590 and 1597–1598. Missing HEAD implementation is a coverage limit, not evidence of a missing control or a new vulnerability.
